title: Why You Must Forgive Misbehaving Students
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin proposes internal, pre-emptive forgiveness of misbehaving students as a distinct classroom management strategy, distinguishing it from verbally saying 'I forgive you' to argue instead for a private internal decision made ahead of any misbehavior. He lists five specific benefits: it relieves stress by removing students' power to get under a teacher's skin; it eliminates resentment, which students can sense and reciprocate even when unspoken; it lets teachers genuinely like their students regardless of daily behavior, triggering the Law of Reciprocity in return; it makes consequences matter more, since students who like their teacher reflect on wrongdoing rather than assigning blame; and it produces measurable wellness benefits like lower anxiety and blood pressure. His practical instruction is that forgiveness is simply a choice, not an emotional achievement to work toward, something to decide each morning as a promise to oneself until it becomes automatic over time.
points: Forgiveness here means an internal, pre-decided stance -- not saying 'I forgive you' aloud, but deciding ahead of time not to let misbehavior get personal.
Withheld forgiveness produces visible resentment that students can sense even when unspoken, and they reciprocate the dislike.
When students like a teacher, they blame themselves for misbehavior rather than blaming the teacher, which is what actually drives improvement.
Forgiveness is framed as a simple daily choice, not an emotional state to labor toward, that becomes automatic with repetition.
quotes: You're going to offer your forgiveness to misbehaving students internally. That is, within yourself.
When you decide to forgive every student for misbehavior ahead of time, before they can even break any rules, they lose the power to get under your skin.
If you can’t forgive students for disrupting your class—ergo, it affects you emotionally—you will resent them. Just seeing them will annoy you.
When students don’t like you, they’ll blame you for their misbehavior instead of reflecting on it and taking responsibility.
Forgiveness makes you happier. Research shows that anxiety drops, blood pressure lowers, and you sleep better.
You just need to decide to offer free and unconditional forgiveness. Think of it as a promise you make to yourself.
